findings.F1: Measured from Monday and Tuesday closes, a coin's unusual 5-day move is higher than from other days: +0.136 of a usual move from Monday (t 3.04, 498 cases) and +0.128 from Tuesday (t 2.71, 475 cases). Monday/Tuesday minus the other days has a Welch t of 4.83 (973 vs 2446 cases). It is positive in all 6 coins (+0.09 to +0.19 against -0.04 to -0.07) and in 7 of 8 years; 2021 is the exception, at 0.004 against 0.156.
findings.F2: Next-day returns split by weekday the same way. After Thursday and Friday closes they are +0.25 % (t 2.64) and +0.31 % (t 3.77). After Monday and Wednesday closes they are -0.24 % (t -2.51) and -0.30 % (t -2.68), about 2480 days each. Thursday/Friday beats Monday/Wednesday in 7 of 8 years; 2022 is the exception, at -0.29 % against -0.17 %. This makes F1 a calendar pattern in the bars, not something the failed-breakout signal explains.
findings.F3: On the backtest's own failed-breakout bars, the coin rose rather than fell. The 385 first-in-cell cases have a mean unusual 5-day move of +0.035 of a usual move (t 0.61). The tercile with the highest breakout volume ratio (mean 2.09) rose most, +0.22 (+2.75 %, t 1.75, 106 cases). The slope of the unusual move on the log volume ratio is +0.196 (t 1.62, 318 cases), the opposite sign to the idea. It also splits by coin: ETH -0.13 and LTC -0.05 in that tercile, ZEC +0.54 and XMR +0.45.
findings.F4: After large up days, the coin kept rising over 5 days. When the 1-day return was 1 to 1.5 of its 20-day volatility, the unusual move was +0.17 (t 2.32, 175 cases). Above 2, it was +0.22 (t 2.13, 110 cases). The middle 1.5–2 bin was only +0.09 (t 0.78) and the 0.5–1 bin was 0.00, so the effect is not cleanly graded. Against the dozens of cuts examined, a t near 2 does not stand out from chance.
findings.F5: Mild down days look like they lead to further falls in one cut but not in others. The second quintile of 1-day return (mean -1.8 %) gave -0.13 of a usual move (t -3.51, 655 cases). Re-cut by volatility-scaled size (z from -1.5 to -0.5), the gap to other days is only Welch t -0.82, and it flips sign across years (2020 +0.37, 2018 -0.35) and coins (ETH +0.14, XRP -0.12). It is not a robust pattern.
findings.F6: Several other angles showed no stable effect: 20-day return, distance to the 20-day high or low, 20-day volatility, volume ratio and close location. Their isolated t values of about ±2 to 2.8 (for example ret20 from -0.2 to -0.1 at -0.119, t -2.47; dist_lo20 2nd quintile at t -2.81) sit in neighbouring bins with opposite signs, and none rises in step from bin to bin.

no_ideas: The only pattern that clearly stands out is the weekday one (F1, F2: Welch t 4.8, consistent across all coins and nearly all years), but it is a calendar condition with no graded strength, which an idea may not be. The graded patterns (F3, F4) do not stand out from chance given how many angles were examined.
